sentences.text:
This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.2068/2014 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Thiruvananthapuram (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 15/07/2019.
The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 11/06/2013 at about 10:00 p.m., while he was riding motorcycle bearing registration no. KL-21/D-5473 through Peroorkada-Nedumangad road and when he reached near Karakulam Enikkara Veterinary Hospital junction, car bearing registration no. KL-22/B-9158 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down as a result of which he 2025:KER:59622 sustained grievous injuries.
Gopakumar.

S vs Ramesh Kumar M.G on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169177769/
2
3. The first respondent/driver and the second respondent/owner remained ex parte.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy, but denying negligence on the part of the first respondent/driver of the offending vehicle.
5. Before the Tribunal, no evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A26 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the first respondent/driver of the offending car resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 11,26,350/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal 2025:KER:59622 calling for an interference by this Court.

8. Heard both sides.
9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner -
Monthly income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that in spite of Exts.A19 and A25 salary certificates being produced, the Tribunal went wrong in fixing the monthly income at 18,000/-.

Therefore, it needs to be enhanced in accordance with Exts.A19 and A25.
9.1.
The incident in this case took place on 11/06/2013.
However, Ext.A19 is for the salary that was drawn by the claim petitioner in November 2015 and Ext.A25 is the salary statement for the salary in November 2018.
Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in not relying on the aforesaid documents for fixing the monthly income.
An amount of 18,000/- was claimed in the claim petition and the said amount has been granted by the Tribunal.
In these circumstances, I do not find any infirmity in the Tribunal fixing the income as 18,000/-.
Admittedly, the claim petitioner was a conductor, KSRTC and he was aged 48 years at the time of the accident.
He retired at the age of 56 years.
From the materials on record there is no evidence to show that any loss of income was caused during the time that he was in service.
However, the injuries that have been caused and the resultant disabilities would certainly affect his earning power after his retirement.

Therefore, for computation of compensation regarding permanent disability,
the notional income can be fixed as 9,000/- per month and the multiplier would be 9.
Percentage of disability

3 11.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that in the light of Ext.A21 disability certificate, which assessed the disability as 60%, the Tribunal went wrong in scaling down the disability to 40% without any justification.
In the light of the injury sustained and the consequential disabilities, the Tribunal ought to have accepted Ext.A21 and fixed the functional disability accordingly.
As the Tribunal erred in assessing the disability, the same needs to be rectified, 2025:KER:59622 goes the argument.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that in the light of the injury sustained, the disability fixed by the Tribunal is reasonable, and hence calls for no interference.

12. The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries - "1. Type III compound fracture # shaft of femur (R)
2. Type III B compound fracture # both bone right leg comminuted 3. Floating knee (R)
4. Contusion over left thigh knee 5. Contusion & abrasion all over the body."
13.

Ext.A21 disability certificate reads thus - "Certified that we the members of the standing Disability Assessment Board at District Medical Board Thiruvananthapuram examined Sri/Smt. S.Gopakumar,
Son/Daughter of Sri.M.Sukumara Pillai residing at Aswathy Bhavan, Mundela P.O.,
Vellarada Village, Vellarada Taluk, Nedumangad, District Thiruvananthapuram and found that He/She is Orthopedics/ENT/Psychiatry/Ophthalmic Handicapped by Type III B compound fracture both bones right leg, Type III compound fracture shaft of femur right floating knee comminuted fracture.

The partial/Permanent /
T e m p o r a r y D i s a b i l i t y i s 6 0 % . ( W o r d s . . . . S i x t y . . . . ) b e l o n g s t o MILD/MODERATE/SEVERE /TOTAL Category."
.A23 are the photographs of the claim petitioner which show the condition of his leg pursuant to the accident.
The fact that the claim petitioner was a Conductor working in KSRTC, is not disputed.

Therefore, the disability caused would certainly have affected the discharge of his duties as a Conductor and therefore, I find that in the light of the injuries sustained ; the disability caused and also taking into account the avocation of the claim petitioner, the functional disability can be assessed as 60%.
Bystander expenses 14.
The accident took place on 11/06/2013.
The claim petitioner was hospitalized for a period of 185 days.
Therefore, he can be awarded compensation at the rate of 300/- per day for a period of 185 Gopakumar.

4 days (300/- x 185 days = 55,500/-).
Compensation for loss of amenities in life 15.
An amount of 4,00,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 96,000/-.

In the light of the injuries sustained and the disabilities caused, I find that an amount of 1,50,000/-
under this head would be just and reasonable.

5 In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 6,00,250/- (total compensation = 17,26,600/-, that is, 11,26,350/-
granted by the Tribunal + 6,00,250/-
granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization (excluding the period of 19 days delay in filing the appeal) and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the compensation with interest and costs before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the compensation amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
